nyc_found: Comptroller's report: "the property tax totaling $37.30 billion (42.1 percent of tax revenues)" — this is Mayor's Office of Management and Budget's ADOPTED FY2027 forecast (FY27 runs July 2026-June 2027, so as of today, Sept 2026, only about two months of it have happened). The same document's Table 12 shows the most recently COMPLETED year, FY2026, at $35,491 million actual/final — 5.1% lower than the figure used. The Comptroller's own independent office forecasts FY2027 property tax at $37.12 billion, not $37.30 billion.
match_found: Starbucks Q4/FY2025 release, Consolidated Statements of Earnings: "Total net revenues" of $37,184.4 million for fiscal year ended September 28, 2025 (an actual, completed-year figure).
conflict: NYC's own FY2026 final property tax collections ($35.491 billion, same source document, Table 12) is the most recent completed-year figure and is materially lower than the $37.30 billion used. Using it: Starbucks $37.18B / NYC $35.49B = 1.048 — Starbucks revenue would exceed NYC property tax by about 5%, not be essentially equal.
finding: The claim reads as present-tense fact ("collects") but the NYC figure is a forward budget forecast for a fiscal year that is not yet complete, compared against Starbucks' actual, already-reported FY2025 revenue — a budget-vs-actual mismatch with no caveat disclosing it. The city's own Comptroller publishes a lower, competing forecast ($37.12B) in the same document, and the last fully completed fiscal year (FY2026) collected notably less ($35.49B), which would flip the comparison to Starbucks being larger.

nyc_found: NYC Tourism press release: "Tourism Spending Increases Year Over Year Generating $55.6 Billion in Direct Spending" — figure covers calendar year 2025, an actual/reported figure.
match_found: IMF DataMapper NGDPD could not be queried for Tunisia specifically without truncation (see finding), but World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD (a close proxy for the same concept) shows Tunisia's 2025 nominal GDP at $57.50 billion, corroborating the file's cited $57.589 billion figure to within 0.15%.
finding: The $57.6 billion match figure is IMF's 2025 estimate for Tunisia, not a finalized national-accounts actual — full-year GDP for a country like Tunisia is not typically finalized this soon after year-end. Nothing in the sentence or a caveat discloses that the country side of the comparison is a projection rather than a settled number, unlike the four county-vs-country GDP pairings later in this batch (n30-33), which do disclose exactly this kind of estimate/actual distinction. The IMF's own site blocks automated per-country queries (returns the full multi-country dataset regardless of the path segment used), so this could not be pinned down to the exact digit against the primary source; World Bank data was used as corroboration instead.

nyc_found: OSC press release: "Wall Street's securities industry bonus pool reached a record $49.2 billion in 2025, up 9% from the previous year... according to New York State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli's annual estimate." Matches file exactly.
match_found: IMF NGDPD for Cambodia, 2025: $49.288 billion per a targeted query that matched the file's cited value exactly.
finding: Both sides of this comparison are estimates, not audited actuals, and neither is disclosed as such. OSC's own release states the $49.2 billion bonus pool is "DiNapoli's annual estimate," built from personal income tax withholding trends rather than actual payroll data, and explicitly says the office "anticipates employment will be revised upward" in later data — the same footnote-level caveat applies to the bonus estimate itself in other years. Cambodia's $49.288 billion is likewise IMF's 2025 projection, not a finalized figure. The claim presents both as settled facts.

nyc_found: NYC Department of Finance press release: "The tentative assessment roll for FY27 shows the total market value of all New York City properties is $1.659 trillion, a 5.4 percent increase from Fiscal Year 2026." Matches file exactly. This is a stock — the city's own estimate of total accumulated property value at a point in time — not a flow.
match_found: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD / IMF NGDPD for Mexico, 2025: $1,832.641 billion, matching the file's cited $1.833 trillion figure to the dollar.
finding: This pairs a stock (the accumulated market value of every parcel of NYC real estate, built up over centuries) against a flow (one year, 2025, of Mexico's national economic output). These are different kinds of quantities that happen to land near the same dollar figure; the existing caveat addresses only that DOF's valuations are the city's own estimates and lag sale prices, not that the comparison itself mixes a wealth stock with an annual income flow. A more like-for-like comparison would be Mexico's national wealth/net worth, not its GDP.
